In frame 5, the notebook is lowered back to about 3.5 m and the viewpoint shifts slightly downward, moving the crouching photographer completely out of the top of the frame while revealing the legs and hands of a seated person in blue far to the camera wearer's right and out of arm's reach (about 4 m away), partially cut off by the bottom-right frame boundary.
depth: The depth map captures the continuous 3D geometry of the studio, showing a smooth brightness gradient along the white floor sheet extending from about 4.5 m below the camera wearer out to 3 m in front, flanked by a studio light stand and stepladder at 3–5 m on the left and a crouching photographer facing away from the wearer at 0.5–1 m on the front-right in front of a circular diffuser (0.5–1 m) and nearby foreground people and furniture (0.2–1.5 m). Far out of arm's reach (3–5 m), the camera wearer's open notebook and left hand holding a pen appear as the brightest distant surfaces at the bottom, alongside a seated person's legs and arms about 4 m to the bottom-right in frames 2 and 5. Across the five frames, as the camera wearer tilts their head downward and lifts the notebook to 4–5 m in frames 3–4 before lowering it to 3–4 m in frame 5, the bright distant notebook plane expands to occlude the near-ground floor and shifts the crouching photographer out of the top of the view. Compared to the RGB strip—where the uniform white floor backdrop and white notebook pages lack texture and blend together—the depth map clearly separates the tilted notebook plane from the overlying floor in frames 1, 2, and 5 and reveals the continuous ground slope. However, the depth map is unreliable on the brightly lit studio lamp on the far left (which saturates to pure white in frames 1, 2, and 5 as if at zero distance), merges the lifted notebook's upper edge into the white floor sheet in frames 3–4, and loses the thin tripod legs and nearby foreground figures in the dark near field.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map outlines discrete regions across the studio layout, separating the distant floor sheet and notebook from the crouching photographer facing away from the camera wearer at 0.5–1 m on the front-right, two nearby standing people 0.5–1.5 m in front of the photographer in frame 2, and studio equipment along the left side 3–5 m away. Far out of the camera wearer's arm's reach (3–5 m), it segments the wearer's left hand holding the pen at the bottom-left in frames 3–5 and right hand in frame 5, as well as the seated neighbor's legs and arm about 4 m to the bottom-right in frame 5. Across the sequence, as the camera tilts steeply downward and the raised notebook occludes the room in frames 3–4 before dropping back down in frame 5, the foreground masks exit the top of the frame while distant person masks appear at the bottom, adding little beyond the RGB view except isolating the tiny, partially occluded standing figures at the top edge of frame 2. The map is highly unreliable in its semantic classifications and object boundaries: it merges the white notebook and floor backdrop into a single massive mask mislabeled as 'bed' in frame 2 and an unlabeled purple polygon in frames 3–4, misclassifies the crouching photographer as 'dog' and 'teddy bear' in frame 2, and labels the circular diffuser, studio light, and red stepladder as 'chair' (frames 1–2) or 'traffic light' and 'umbrella' (frame 5). It also completely misses the floor sheet and distant notebook in frames 1 and 5, fails to detect the seated neighbor's limbs in frame 2, and omits the pen and thin tripod stands across all frames.
pose: The body and hand skeleton map isolates only the human keypoints of the crouching photographer located 0.5–1 m in front and slightly to the right of the camera wearer near the near edge of the white floor sheet. In frames 1 and 2, the compact yellow body skeleton shows the photographer squatting low to the floor with bent knees, elbows tucked in out of arm's reach of their own upper body and camera, and head and shoulders angled directly away from the camera wearer. Across the five frames, as the camera wearer pitches their view downward toward the notebook, the photographer's skeleton shifts upward toward the top-right from frame 1 to frame 2, is clipped by the upper frame boundary to just a small cluster of foot keypoints at the top-right of frame 3, and disappears completely out of view in frames 4 and 5. Compared to the RGB strip, the skeleton overlay makes the photographer's folded limb geometry and rear-facing posture explicit despite dark clothing and occlusion of their face by the handheld camera. However, the map is unreliable everywhere else in the scene: it fails to detect any magenta hand skeletons—completely missing the camera wearer's own hands holding the notebook and pen at 3–5 m in frames 3–5—and misses both the seated person's legs and arms at 4 m on the bottom-right (frames 2 and 5) and the two standing people 0.5–1.5 m in the foreground (frames 1–2).
